subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-class per-model memory indexes for safe embedding failover now, and should that contract live in bundled memory-core, a plugin API extension, or an external memory plugin?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a narrow bug fix; it adds config surface, persistent data-model changes, ingestion coordination, provider-routing policy, observability, and doctor migration requirements that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design multi-index memory
options.body: Sponsor a design/implementation plan for per-model indexes, canonical chunk state, active/fallback index routing, migration, and status surfaces.

options.title: Route to plugin API or external plugin
options.body: If maintainers want this outside bundled memory-core, define the missing plugin seam and let an external memory plugin own multi-index failover.

options.title: Decline core scope
options.body: Close the core request if maintainers decide resilient multi-index embedding failover belongs in a separate memory plugin or external architecture.

recommendation.title: Design multi-index memory
recommendation.body: Sponsor a design/implementation plan for per-model indexes, canonical chunk state, active/fallback index routing, migration, and status surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is currently assigned to osolmaz, and recent provider-failure memory work makes this the best available owner for the product/API choice.
